description: Walk a non-empty Scheme list by adding its head (car L) to the recursive sum of its tail (cdr L).
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 1-4 define `sumlist` on a list `L`. Line 3 tests `(null? (cdr L))`: when the tail `(cdr L)` is empty, `L` has only one element left and line 4 returns `(car L)`.
When `(cdr L)` is non-empty, line 5 evaluates `(+ (car L) (sumlist (cdr L)))`, adding the first element `(car L)` to the sum of the remaining elements `(cdr L)`.
Notice how `car` and `cdr` split the list on line 5. `(car L)` extracts the front item for `+`. `(cdr L)` passes a shorter list to the recursive `sumlist` call until `(cdr L)` becomes `'()`.

steps.answer: The base case receives `'(3)`, where `(cdr '(3))` is `'()` and `(car '(3))` returns `3`; the pending additions `(+ 1 (+ 2 3))` then return `6`.
steps.question: When `(sumlist (list 1 2 3))` runs on line 7, what list reaches the base case where `(null? (cdr L))` is `#t`? What total does the outer `+` return?

title: Summing a List Recursively with car and cdr
